long_biography.plain_text:
Andreas Pittas was born in Limassol in April 1943. He studied medicine in Austria, earned a doctorate, and pursued postgraduate training in pharmacology and pharmaceutical medicine before adding business administration and marketing. In 1976 he founded Medochemie with eight employees and three machines. The Limassol company grew into an international manufacturer of generic medicines, while Pittas remained its founder and executive chairman.

Pittas has also served Cypriot business, science and culture through leadership roles beyond Medochemie. He twice chaired the Cyprus Employers and Industrialists Federation and now chairs the executive committee of the Cyprus Institute. His support for cultural heritage includes the Andreas Pittas Art Characterization Laboratories and projects focused on the history of Limassol. He is president of Limassol's European Capital of Culture campaign, and national, scientific and civic institutions have recognised his contributions to industry, research and public life.
